title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes accompanying the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals and Dieudonné theory. The previous page studied isogeny classes of abelian surfaces of supersingular or mixed formal type, and the locus in moduli of varieties isogenous to E×F. This page, item 2), asks whether every formal group over a field k can be realised inside the formal group of an abelian variety over k.

Claim. In general, a formal group G over k cannot be realised as a formal subgroup of Â, the formal completion of an abelian variety A defined over k. This holds even for a form of G_{1,1} (the one-dimensional formal group of height 2, i.e. the supersingular one). It holds even if one allows a finite extension of k, or an extension of finite type.

Example.
- Take k = F_q and E a supersingular elliptic curve with all its endomorphisms defined over k (for instance q = p^{2m} with Frobenius φ = ±p^m, which is central).
- Put G_0 = Ê.
- By Deuring and Tate, End(G_0) ≅ End(E)⊗_Z Z_p = 𝒜. Here End(E) is a maximal order in the quaternion algebra over Q ramified at p and ∞. 𝒜 is the maximal order O_D of the quaternion division algebra D over Q_p.
- Since the endomorphisms are defined over k, π_1(k) = Ẑ acts trivially on End. So the k-forms of G_0 are classified by H^1(Ẑ, O_D^×), i.e. by conjugacy classes of units θ.
- Concretely, twisting G_0 by θ replaces the q-Frobenius φ by φ' = θφ.

Obstruction. Suppose the twisted group embeds as a formal subgroup of Â with A an abelian variety over k. Then the characteristic polynomial of φ' on its Dieudonné module divides that of the q-Frobenius of A. By Weil's theorem that polynomial has coefficients in Z and its roots are q-Weil numbers. Hence det φ' = det φ · det θ (det = reduced norm) must be an algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have the same absolute value. Therefore det θ = Nrd(θ) must be an algebraic number all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1.

Conclusion. The next page notes that it is easy to choose θ violating this. The reduced norm O_D^× → Z_p^× is surjective, so one can take Nrd(θ) transcendental. This gives uncountably many forms of G_{1,1} over F_q (and over finite or finite-type extensions) that do not come from any abelian variety. Equivalently, only countably many Frobenius characteristic polynomials come from abelian varieties, while the forms of G_{1,1} form a continuum.
errors: The quaternion algebras are over Q resp. Q_p; the maximal orders lie over Z resp. Z_p. The phrase 'algèbres de quaternions sur Z resp. Z_p' is loose wording.
If all endomorphisms of E are defined over k, then Π_1(k) acts trivially on End(E), not faithfully. The word read as 'fidèlement' is likely 'trivialement'; see corrections.

The necessary condition is incomplete. Not only det φ' but the whole characteristic polynomial of θφ (including the trace, i.e. Trd(θ)·p^m) must have algebraic, Weil-type roots. The determinant condition alone suffices for the counterexample, so this does not affect the conclusion.

Over an algebraically closed k, G_{1,1} is unique and equals Ê for any supersingular E. The opening 'par ex. alg. clos' must therefore refer to non-trivial forms or to higher-dimensional groups; the actual example is over a finite field.

ideas.what: End(Ê) ≅ End(E)⊗Z_p is the maximal order of the quaternion division algebra over Q_p, for E supersingular with all endomorphisms defined over k
ideas.modern_name: Deuring's theorem / Tate's isogeny theorem (p-adic version)

ideas.what: Forms of a formal group over F_q obtained by twisting the Frobenius by an automorphism θ (φ' = θφ)
ideas.modern_name: Galois twisting / descent of p-divisible groups; H^1(Ẑ, Aut)
ideas.where_published: possibly in the spirit of 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974), but not this example specifically

ideas.what: Not every formal group / p-divisible group over a finite field comes from an abelian variety, because the Weil conjectures force Frobenius eigenvalues to be q-Weil numbers (algebraic)
ideas.modern_name: algebraicity obstruction; Honda–Tate theory characterises the isocrystals coming from abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Tate (1966), Honda (1968); Oort for related questions

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early (1966) explicit argument that forms of G_{1,1} over finite fields generally do not come from abelian varieties, via twisting by quaternion units with non-algebraic reduced norm. The underlying fact is standard folklore (countability, Weil numbers, Honda–Tate), so nothing here would be new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Π = Π_1(k) opère fidèlement' is likely 'opère trivialement' (all endomorphisms defined over k).
'ordres maximaux dans algèbres de quaternions sur Z resp. Z_p' should be understood as over Q resp. Q_p.
'tordre G_0 par un quelconque auto θ de 𝒜' means an arbitrary automorphism, i.e. a unit θ ∈ 𝒜^×.
Next page: 'det Θ ne soit pas nilpotent' is very likely 'ne soit pas algébrique' (or similar), matching the condition at the end of this page.
